messages:
Sam (Support): FYI escalation from AcmeCorp - intermittent 401s, message 'invalid signature'. Happening since their scheduled key rotation this morning.
Maya (sec-oncall): pls paste logs and sample token
Sam (Support): log snippets:
```
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z ERROR auth verify failed kid=kp_abc reason=signature_mismatch
2026-03-12T09:12:09Z WARN jwks cache stale for issuer=https://idp.acmecorp.com/.well-known/jwks.json
```
Sam (Support): curl they used to call our API:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <JWT_FROM_ACME>' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/models
```
Eric (API): can we see the token header (kid) base64-decoded? Also what does our jwks fetch record show
Sam (Support): header: { kid: kp_rotated_v2, alg: RS256 }
Eli (SRE): looks like their IdP rotated keys at 09:11. Our JWKS cache TTL is 10m and we cache successful fetches. If rotation happened, clients with tokens signed by new key should pass; tokens signed by old key should still validate via old key unless rotated out of JWKS set.
Maya (sec-oncall): signature_mismatch + kid present normally means we tried to verify with a public key that didn't match token's actual signing key. Could be stale JWKS or our code using cached key material keyed by kid but not updating after fetch failure.
Sam (Support): repro notes from customer: repeated 401 for ~7 minutes after rotation, then success.
Eric (API): hypothesis: our JWKS fetch failed due to temporary 403 from their IdP during rotation, so we retained older JWKS; token carried a new kid that isn't in our cached set -> we fallback to trying to verify using previous key (or pick up mismatch). Ideally we should re-fetch JWKS on unknown kid or on signature failure.
Maya (sec-oncall): quick mitigation: add retry-on-unknown-kid path: on verify failure if kid not found or signature_mismatch, trigger async JWKS refresh and reverify once. Also short-term operational action: ask support to flush jwks cache for that tenant in our console.
Eli (SRE): can add endpoint to invalidate jwks cache per-issuer. We already have internal endpoint /internal/cache/flush?issuer=...
Sam (Support): customer wants "what happened" and root cause; will propose we flushed cache and bumped TTL to 1m as workaround.
Eric (API): longer term: change caching logic: - on unknown kid: immediate fetch (blocking) with backoff; - on signature_mismatch: fetch then reverify once; - set default ttl to 1m for external IdPs with rotate-enabled flag.
Maya (sec-oncall): also check clock skew. Their logs show tokens exp around 09:12:10Z. If clocks are off, validate exp/nbf failures. Our verifier currently allows 30s skew; maybe increase to 60s for compatibility, but document risk.
Sam (Support): repro steps for eng to reproduce in staging:
1) run a local simple IdP that rotates keys at t0+30s.
2) issue token signed with new key immediately after rotation with kid=new.
3) have our verifier fetch JWKS and then simulate fetch error (return 500) for the next minute to emulate transient IdP failure.
4) call API -> should see 401 signature_mismatch until cache refreshed.
I attached commands:
```
# generate keys, start tiny idp (pseudo)
openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -out key_old.pem -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048
openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -out key_new.pem -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048
# sign jwt with key_new using your usual tooling (jwt-cli / jose) with kid=kp_rotated_v2 and exp ~ now+60s
```
Eli (SRE): assigned to me to add cache-flush admin endpoint and to add re-fetch on unknown kid. Eric can own verifier changes.
Eric (API): will add unit tests + integration test that simulates JWKS 5xx between rotation window.
Maya (sec-oncall): security note: confirm we don't accept tokens with expired 'exp' due to larger clock skew. Add a config knob per-tenant.
Sam (Support): customer update: we flushed their cache, they report 0 failures after that. they'll keep monitoring.
Maya (sec-oncall): followups: PR for re-fetch logic, ops endpoint, and a short runbook for support to escalate next time. I'll open a ticket and tag @runbooks.
CI Bot: deploy scheduled for staging 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC - will run integration test.
Sam (Support): thanks all :thumbsup:
